Ellama

Ellama is an Emacs frontend for chatting with large language models via llm-ollama. Models run locally through Ollama – no cloud API needed.

  • jdormit/emacs-opencode (https://github.com/jdormit/emacs-opencode) — native client: M-x opencode for sessions, opencode-ask for prompts, session management, and deep Emacs integration via emacs-mcp-server (read buffers, eval elisp, run compile commands)
  • colobas/opencode.el (https://github.com/colobas/opencode.el) — port of my tools into gptel with LSP integration, diagnostics, symbol navigation, and agent presets
  • rogs/opencode.el (https://git.rogs.me/rogs/opencode.el) — lightweight terminal-based integration using vterm or shell-mode with a transient menu
  • xenodium/agent-shell (https://github.com/xenodium/agent-shell) — ACP-based native Emacs buffer for LLM agents, supports OpenCode as a backend
  • tninja/ai-code-interface.el (https://github.com/tninja/ai-code-interface.el) — unified interface wrapping multiple CLI agents including OpenCode

Architecture note:* Ellama connects directly to Ollama

(http://127.0.0.1:11434). Unlike gptel, it does not route through the MCP server (the bottino/mcp FastAPI agent), so it has no access to the MCP tools (ollama_list_models, camera_describe_scene, etc.) or the MCP tool-call loop.

However, emacs.el now discovers models dynamically by querying Ollama's /api/tags endpoint (through the same nginx that proxies MCP).Set MY_OLLAMA_URL env var to route discovery through the MCP server, e.g. http://bottino:11434. No more hardcoded model list — when you pull a new model in Ollama, it appears in M-x ellama-switch-provider automatically (after a 3-second idle delay at startup, or instantly via M-x my-ellama-refresh-providers).

# blender twin - Documentation & Web Publishing

This folder contains all the knowledge base and presentation for the Jetson CV Digital Twin project.

## Purpose

- **knowledge base**: Raw markdown documentation about hardware, software, add-ons, packages, and system components
- **html**: Converted web pages and slides for public presentation
- **plan**: Agentic orchestration for documentation generation
- **script**: Tools to convert markdown to HTML slides and blog posts
- **static_html**: Final web pages ready for publishing

## Documentation Pipeline

```
knowledge_base/*.md ─[./script/convert_md.sh]──> static_html/*.html
                      │                          │
                      ▼                          ▼
                  mermaid/diagrams           Blog posts index
```

### Workflow

1. `knowledge_base/*.md` - Write documentation in markdown
2. `script/org2slide.py` - Convert `.org` presentations to HTML slides
3. `script/convert_md.sh` - Standard markdown to HTML conversion
4. `static_html/` - Ready-to-publish web pages

## Files to Convert

### Core Documentation (priority order)

1. **project_details.md** - Main README
   - Architecture overview
   - Hardware stack
   - Digital twin capabilities

2. **agent_configs/** - MCP agent documentation
   - System policies
   - Agent roles
   - Available skills

3. **hardware_docs/** - Hardware architecture
   - Jetson targets
   - Camera modules
   - IoT devices

4. **software_docs/** - System components
   - Vision pipeline
   - FEM solver
   - Optimization engines

### Presentation Files

- `org2slide.py` - Converts org-mode to HTML slides
- `slide_presentation.org` - Sample presentation file

### HTML Pages

```
static_html/
├── index.html              # Landing page
├── architecture.html       # Architecture diagrams
├── hardware.html           # Hardware specifications
├── software.html           # Software components

    └── js/

- **icon/** - SVG icons for web elements

### 1. Create Documentation

Write your markdown in `knowledge_base/`:

```bash
mkdir -p knowledge_base/{hardware,software,agents}
cd knowledge_base
echo "# My Component" > my_component.md
```

### 2. Generate Web Pages

```bash
# Convert markdown to HTML
./script/convert_md.sh knowledge_base/*.md

# Generate presentation slides
python3 ./script/org2slide.py slide_presentation.org

# Build all static content
./script/generate_diagrams.sh
```

### 3. Publish

```bash
cd static_html
git add .
git commit -m "update documentation"
git push
```

Ellama

Ellama is an Emacs frontend for chatting with large language models via llm-ollama. Models run locally through Ollama – no cloud API needed.

  • jdormit/emacs-opencode (https://github.com/jdormit/emacs-opencode) — native client: M-x opencode for sessions, opencode-ask for prompts, session management, and deep Emacs integration via emacs-mcp-server (read buffers, eval elisp, run compile commands)
  • colobas/opencode.el (https://github.com/colobas/opencode.el) — port of my tools into gptel with LSP integration, diagnostics, symbol navigation, and agent presets
  • rogs/opencode.el (https://git.rogs.me/rogs/opencode.el) — lightweight terminal-based integration using vterm or shell-mode with a transient menu
  • xenodium/agent-shell (https://github.com/xenodium/agent-shell) — ACP-based native Emacs buffer for LLM agents, supports OpenCode as a backend
  • tninja/ai-code-interface.el (https://github.com/tninja/ai-code-interface.el) — unified interface wrapping multiple CLI agents including OpenCode

Architecture note:* Ellama connects directly to Ollama

(http://127.0.0.1:11434). Unlike gptel, it does not route through the MCP server (the bottino/mcp FastAPI agent), so it has no access to the MCP tools (ollama_list_models, camera_describe_scene, etc.) or the MCP tool-call loop.

However, emacs.el now discovers models dynamically by querying Ollama's /api/tags endpoint (through the same nginx that proxies MCP).Set MY_OLLAMA_URL env var to route discovery through the MCP server, e.g. http://bottino:11434. No more hardcoded model list — when you pull a new model in Ollama, it appears in M-x ellama-switch-provider automatically (after a 3-second idle delay at startup, or instantly via M-x my-ellama-refresh-providers).

Usage

Start a chat

C-c e or M-x ellama

This opens a chat buffer in full frame. Type your message, then C-c C-c to send.

Coding assistant

M-x ellama-code or select the coding provider interactively.

Ask for code, refactoring, or debugging help. The coding provider uses qwen2.5-coder:3b with 32K context – suitable for whole functions or small files.

Summarize text

Select a region, then M-x ellama-summarize or M-x ellama-summarize-region. Ellama will summarize the selected text using the summarization provider.

Translate text

M-x ellama-translate – prompts for target language, then translates the current region or buffer.

Extract structured data

M-x ellama-extract – extracts structured information from text (e.g. names, dates, quantities from free-form text).

Use a different model

M-x ellama-switch-provider – pick from zephyr, mistral, mixtral, or any other provider you define.

Display behaviour

  • Chat buffer opens in full frame (display-buffer-full-frame).
  • Instant (inline) responses appear at the bottom (display-buffer-at-bottom).
  • Header line shows ellama context and session ID in all buffers (ellama-context-header-line-global-mode, ellama-session-header-line-global-mode).

  • Ollama running locally (default: http://127.0.0.1:11434)

state = {
